thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — onboarding llama2-13b-quant-8bit: our eval suite shows a small but consistent drop on tokenization-sensitive tasks (diacritics + weird whitespace).

aj: Oof. Any minimal repro?

maria: Minimal repro attached inline. Observe how HF tokenizer and our converted tokenizer disagree because of pre-tokenizer/normalizer differences and byte-fallback behavior.

maria: Example string: `"fiancé\u00A0— café"` (NBSP between words and an em-dash).

maria: HF (from_pretrained) encode result (fast):
```
['fi', 'anç', 'é', 'Ġ—', 'Ġcaf', 'é']  # token counts: 6
```

maria: Converted-to-redwood tokenizer (current conversion pipeline) encode result:
```
['fiancé', 'Ġ—', 'Ġcafé']  # token counts: 3
```

maria: That mismatch breaks a few eval prompts where we expect prefix tokens to align (generation seeding + KV cache reuse).

aj: Two likely places: unicode normalizer (NFC vs NFKC) and pre-tokenizer whitespace splitting (add_prefix_space vs byte-level behavior). Also check byte fallback table: if tokenizer falls back to bytes for unknowns we can end up splitting NBSP differently.

aj: Can you dump tokenizer.json from both HF and converted artifacts? particularly `normalizer`, `pre_tokenizer`, and `byte_fallback`/`backend` fields.

maria: Yep, I saved both. HF tokenizer.json has `normalizer: {"type":"NFC"}` and `pre_tokenizer: {"type":"whitespace_split"}`; our conversion ended up with `normalizer: null` and `pre_tokenizer: {"type":"byte_level"}` (oops).

sam: That explains it. byte_level will collapse NBSP vs regular space differently and also combine diacritics into single codepoints vs multiple tokens depending on normalization.

maria: I ran a quick diff on token ids for a small corpus; the quantized model plus converted tokenizer shows higher perplexity by ~2-3% on diacritic-heavy evals. Not huge but reproducible.

aj: Hypothesis: conversion script currently copies merges/vocab but omits the tokenizer normalizer and pre-tokenizer metadata when the HF tokenizer is "fast" vs our expected format. We should: 1) preserve normalizer (explicit NFC/NFKC), 2) keep whitespace pre-tokenizer if present, 3) preserve byte_fallback flag.

sam: Can we add a unit test to catch this class of mismatch? e.g., take a small set of strings with NBSP, ZWJ, zero-width non-joiner, diacritics and compare token sequences between HF raw tokenizer and converted artifact. Fail the build if mismatch > threshold.

maria: Yea I'll add eng-ml/tests/test_tokenizer_compat.py with a table of 20 edge cases. I'll also add an entry to model-onboarding checklist: "assert normalizer + pre_tokenizer parity".

aj: Also be mindful of `add_prefix_space` used by some chat-style tokenizers — conversions to/from byte-level can silently flip that behavior and break chat templates where we rely on leading space to indicate separation.

maria: Good call. I noticed one chat template that started generating truncated completions after conversion; turned out `add_prefix_space` was missing so the chat wrap didn't re-tokenize as expected.

sam: For immediate mitigation: can we run a conversion path that forces the tokenizer to save `tokenizer.json` from HF (fast tokenizer) and load that directly in Redwood's loader instead of reconstructing from vocab+merges? That should preserve pre-tokenizer/normalizer semantics.

aj: Yes — prefer `tokenizer.save_pretrained(...)` on HF side and ingest that artifact. If we must reconstruct, ensure we copy `normalizer`, `pre_tokenizer`, `post_processor`, and `byte_fallback` sections.

maria: I'll patch the conversion script and kick off a quant-run against the failing evals. Also adding regression alert in the eval dashboard so we get notified if tokenization drift > 1% on these tests.

eval-bot: Scheduled run: tokenizer-compat-repro on llama2-13b-quant-8bit queued by maria.

sam: Thanks — once the unit test and conversion patch land we'll re-run full quant rollout. If the patch is trivial I'll backport to the last two onboarding merges.

maria: Plan: PR with tests + conversion patch today, follow-up quant runs tomorrow. tagging @aj for review. :+1:

aj: Will review. Also log this under the model-onboarding doc (link to checklist) so PMs and SEs are aware. :memo:

maria: One more oddity I saw: zero-width joiner (ZWJ, U+200D) in some emoji sequences got removed by our conversion normalizer — causing emoji tokens to split and change token id alignment in prompts that mix text+emoji. Another small test to add.

sam: Good catch. Add ZWJ, ZWNJ, NBSP, AND narrow no-break space cases to the suite.

maria: OK will do. I'll post the PR link here when ready.

aj: Thanks team.
